Given equation of curves are

& x^2=8 y \\

x & =4

\begin{array}{ll}
\Rightarrow & x^3=64 \\
\Rightarrow & x=4

On substituting $x=4$ in Eq. (ii), we get $y=2$

Now, let $m_1$ be the slope of tangent to the curve (i) at point $(4,2)$ and $m_2$ be the slope of tangent to the curve (ii) at point $(4,2)$

Now, the angle $\theta$ between the curves is given by

& \tan \theta=\left(\frac{m_2-m_1}{1+m_1 m_2}\right) \\
& =\left(\frac{\frac{-1}{2}-1}{1-\frac{1}{2}}\right)=\left(\frac{\frac{-3}{2}}{\frac{1}{2}}\right) \\

questions.q: An amplitude modulated signal consists of a message signal of frequency $1 \mathrm{KHz}$ and peak voltage of $5 \mathrm{~V}$, modulating a carrier frequency of $1 \mathrm{MHz}$ and peak voltage of $15 \mathrm{~V}$. The correct description of this signal is
questions.solution:
Given,
Frequency of message signal $\left(f_m\right)=1 \mathrm{KHz}$
$=1 \times 10^3 \mathrm{~Hz}$
Peak voltage of message signal $\left(E_m\right)=5 \mathrm{~V}$
Carrier frequency $\left\langle f_c\right\rangle=1 \mathrm{MHz}=1 \times 10^6 \mathrm{~Hz}$
Peak voltage of carrier $\left(E_c\right)=15 \mathrm{~V}$
We know that, The equation of amplitude modulated wave is given by
$\begin{aligned} \\ e(t) & =E_c\left[1+\frac{E_m}{E_o} \sin \omega_m t\right] \sin \omega_c t \\ \\ & =E_c\left[1+\frac{E_m}{E_o} \sin \left(2 \pi f_m\right)\right] \sin 2 \pi f_c t \\ \\ & =15\left[1+\frac{5}{15} \sin \left(2 \pi \times 10^3\right)\right] \sin 2 \pi \times 10^6 t \\ \\ & =15\left[1+\frac{1}{3} \sin \left(2 \pi 10^3 t\right)\right] \sin \left(2 \pi 10^6 t\right) \\ \end{aligned}$

questions.q: The energy that should be added to an electron to reduce its de-Broglie wavelength from $1 \mathrm{~nm}$ to $0.5 \mathrm{~nm}$ is
questions.solution:
We know that,
We have, $\lambda=\frac{h}{\sqrt{2 m k}}\therefore$ Kinetic energy $(K E) \propto \frac{1}{\lambda^2}$
Hence,

\frac{K E_2}{K E_1}=\left(\frac{\lambda_1}{\lambda_2}\right)^2

Here, $\lambda_1=1 \mathrm{~nm}$
\begin{aligned}
\lambda_2 & =0.5 \mathrm{~nm} \\
\frac{K E_2}{K E_1} & =\left(\frac{1}{0.5}\right)^2 \\
K E_2 & =4 K E_1
\end{aligned}

Hence, the kinetic energy is increases three times.

\triangle K E=3 K E_1
